newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher, seen stabilising.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Friday due to increasing liquidity demand before the February 7 Chinese lunar new year, but dealers expected the rates to stabilise at the current levels.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.902 percent against Thursday's 5.707 close, with commercial paper slightly firmer to 5.85-6.00 from 5.75-6.00.
Dealers did not expect further huge gains in the rates as the central bank has been conducting open market operations to inject funds into the banking system recently.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.1340-1350 percent.
